core_obligations: Invoke the colimit lemmas for finitely presented modules, which say in particular that the category of finitely presented R-modules is the colimit of the categories of finitely presented R_i-modules (proof lines 19288-19293).

Use that finite projective modules are summands of finite free modules to conclude the same colimit statement for finite projective modules, which by the definition of perfect objects proves part (1) (proof lines 19293-19297).
For part (2), represent K_0 by a bounded complex K_0^bullet of finite projective R_0-modules and L_0 by a K-flat complex L_0^bullet (proof lines 19300-19302).

Use the description of maps out of a projective complex to rewrite Hom_{D(R)}(K_0 tensor^L R, L_0 tensor^L R) as the Hom in the homotopy category between the base-changed complexes, and similarly with R replaced by R_i (proof lines 19303-19310).

Since only finitely many terms occur and each Hom_R(K_0^p tensor R, L_0^q tensor R) is the filtered colimit over i of Hom_{R_i}(K_0^p tensor R_i, L_0^q tensor R_i), use exactness of filtered colimits to conclude part (2) (proof lines 19310-19321).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a filtered colimit of rings R = colim_{i in I} R_i and makes two assertions: first, that given a perfect K in D(R) there is a stage i and a perfect K_i in D(R_i) whose derived base change to R recovers K; and second, that for a fixed stage 0 and objects K_0 (perfect) and L_0 in D(R_0), the Hom group in D(R) between their base changes is the filtered colimit over i >= 0 of the corresponding Hom groups over R_i (source lines 19267-19285). The proof of part (1) is a descent argument: the cited colimit lemmas say that the category of finitely presented R-modules is the colimit of the categories of finitely presented R_i-modules, and since finite projective modules are characterised as summands of finite free modules the same holds for the category of finite projective modules, which by the definition of perfect objects gives (1) (proof lines 19287-19297). Part (2) is the substantive computation: the proof represents K_0 by a bounded complex K_0^bullet of finite projective R_0-modules and L_0 by a K-flat complex L_0^bullet, and uses the description of maps out of a projective complex to rewrite the Hom in D(R) as the Hom in the homotopy category between the two base-changed complexes (proof lines 19300-19310). Since only finitely many terms occur, and since each Hom_R(K_0^p tensor R, L_0^q tensor R) is the filtered colimit over i of Hom_{R_i}(K_0^p tensor R_i, L_0^q tensor R_i) by the cited lemmas, exactness of filtered colimits gives (2) (proof lines 19310-19321). The non-routine content is the two-step rewriting of the Hom group, first into the homotopy category and then into a filtered colimit of finite data.
